title: Transparent cutover plan with silent backfill, dual-write throttling, and customer surge protections
creator: Maya Chen
description: Operational runbook for migrating accounts from RBAC v1 -> RBAC v2 with minimal disruption. Covers silent backfill strategy, dual-write modes, throttling heuristics, audit-log continuity, SSO/SAML mapping verification, admin control parity checks, monitoring, and staged customer notifications.
background: RBAC v2 introduces role scoping changes and richer admin controls. Previous partial migrations surfaced issues: race conditions in role assignment, gaps in audit trails during schema swaps, and SSO mapping mismatches for customers with custom attribute transforms. This ticket consolidates lessons from ENG-4921 and ENG-6832 and provides an actionable, low-risk cutover plan.
goals: Achieve >99.9% request success during cutover window
Preserve audit log continuity (no gaps or duplicate entries) for compliance audits
Avoid permission regressions for admin/console users
Provide clear rollback gates and automated safety checks
Communicate schedule and impact to affected customers with targeted messaging
migration_strategy: Phase 0: Pre-cutover validations (schema compatibility, integration tests, smoke runs against canary dataset)
Phase 1: Enable dual-write (write to v1 and v2) in 'silent' mode for 7 days with read-from-v1 behavior
Phase 2: Run silent backfill to populate v2 authoritative state using throttled workers
Phase 3: Canary cutover for low-traffic orgs (1% of traffic) with read fallback to v1
Phase 4: Progressive ramp to full read-from-v2 with monitoring gates
Phase 5: Dual-write disabled after a verification window and archival of v1 state
backfill_strategy: Perform incremental, idempotent backfill jobs keyed by org_id and last_updated timestamp
Use checkpointed workers (kafka checkpoints) to allow resume on failure
Apply rate limits per org to avoid DB hotspots; throttling parameters: initial 50 qps per worker, max 500 qps cluster-wide
Run backfill in read-replica-friendly mode to avoid primary load spikes
Detect and record conflicts where v1 has manual admin overrides; surface to SME queue for manual reconciliation
dual_write_throttling_and_safety: Dual-write always writes to v1 and v2 but includes per-org leaky-bucket throttles
Reject path includes detailed error codes to trigger automated retry and alerting (ERROR_RBAC_WRITE_THROTTLE)
Expose real-time dual-write success metrics in console (per-org failure rate, latency, backlog)
If consecutive dual-write failures > 0.5% for 10 minutes, automatically pause dual-write and open PagerDuty incident
Provide a manual 'force-sync' operation in admin console for high-priority orgs behind retries
audit_log_migration: Stream audit events from application layer to audit-log topic with schema version tags (v1, v2)
Maintain event_id dedup keys so backfilled events are not duplicated in downstream log sinks
During dual-write, ensure each audit event references both v1_resource_id and v2_resource_id when available
Apply end-to-end test that replays 72 hours of production traffic against a dry-run consumer to detect missing events
Coordinate with Compliance to run sample export for two customers pre- and post-cutover
sso_mapping_and_identity: Pre-validate SAML/SCIM mappings: run a dry-match job to verify attribute transforms used by customers
Maintain a mapping table for legacy_role_name -> v2_role_slug with manual overrides per org
For orgs with complex mappers, schedule SME-led migration and customer-facing testing window
Add signal hooks in login flow to surface mapping warnings in logs but not block auth during cutover
Plan a follow-up for SCIM provisioning parity validation within 48 hours of cutover
admin_controls_validation: Feature-flag full admin UI for a subset of internal admin users to validate control parity
Run scripted permission matrices comparing v1 and v2 for top 50 admin flows
Ensure RBAC audit queries (who can approve invites, who can change billing) return identical results
Add a 'permission-diff' endpoint for support tooling that highlights differences for an org
Lock down destructive admin operations (e.g., bulk user delete) behind additional confirmation and a safety check during first 72 hours of cutover
monitoring_and_slo_checks: Dashboards: dual-write success rate, backfill backlog, per-org permission mismatch rate, audit-event gap rate
Alerting: PagerDuty for dual-write pause, SLO breach alarms for 1m P99 latency increase > 20%
Runbooks: link to runbook that describes automated rollback steps and manual reconciliation play
Synthetic tests: hourly end-to-end permission checks across 100 seeded orgs (admin and user flows)
Data quality: nightly regression job that compares a sample of 10k permission checks v1 vs v2
rollback_criteria_and_process: Automatic rollback triggers: dual-write failure rate > 0.5% for 30m, audit-gap detected > 100 events/min sustained for 10m, or permission-diff rate > 2% for paid orgs
Rollback steps: pause reads-from-v2, revert read path to v1, re-enable dual-write if safe, notify customers and SLT
Post-rollback: create incident report, start reconciliation backfill with 'repair' mode, schedule postmortem within 72 hours
Customer rollback windows: honor org opt-outs; maintain ability to roll specific orgs back independently
customer_communications: Audience segmentation: internal (support, sales, CSM), low-impact customers, high-risk customers (SAML customizations, large orgs)
Pre-cutover notices: 2 weeks + 48 hours + 2 hours before each major phase via email and in-console banner
Support script: doc for Support to triage permission regressions; include canned messages and steps to escalate
Post-cutover validation request: invite customers to validate admin flows during a 72-hour window and provide bug-reporting link
Status page: publish planned windows and live progress; link to incident channel for critical issues
rollout_timeline: 2026-03-15: Start dual-write silent mode for 7 days
2026-03-22: Begin controlled backfill and canary reads for 1% orgs
2026-03-25: Expand to 10% reads if canary metrics pass
2026-03-28: Full read ramp and disable dual-write verification window
2026-03-31: Finalize migration, deprecate v1 write endpoints, archive v1 state for 90 days
notes: Key risk: customers with programmatic admin tooling (scripts relying on legacy role names) may see subtle failures; coordinate with CSMs to surface those orgs
We will enforce a conservative throttle and surface a migration-unsafe label for orgs that require bespoke migration plans
Plan to keep read-only v1 endpoints available for 90 days for forensic queries and compliance exports
